text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses training data—examples that already have correct answers—to build a model. For instance, if you show a model photos of cats and dogs labeled correctly, it learns the patterns that distinguish them. Once the model is trained, it can make predictions on new, unseen photos. The quality of these predictions is measured by accuracy, which tells us how often the model is correct. Improving accuracy usually requires more or better training data, as well as fine-tuning the model’s parameters.
